about: Shared classification corpus «event × recipient → reason» (sk-303.13, plan task T002;
extended by sk-303.14 / T005).
The SAME file must be executed by THREE independent consumers: the runtime classifier
notifications.Classify (see reason_corpus_test.go), the SQL projection of the migration (introduced in 000041,
edition 2 — in 000045; see migrations/migration_000041_test.go) and the reason projection in the delivery
tract (internal/outbox/push_classification_parity_test.go).
There cannot be one executable function here — the migration does not call application code, and the tract
answers a different question («reason → what the person will see»), — so implementation equivalence
is held precisely by this set of regressions. The tract projection is checked by a SEPARATE assertion:
agreement of the first two says nothing about it.
Case fields:
id        — stable identifier of the case (used in subtest names);
note      — where the case comes from: a row of the spec table or a named edge;
event     — facts of the event: type, changedFields, assigneeCleared, explicitAccept, staleLockRelease,
outcomeChanged (sk-489: the close INCIDENTALLY changed the outcome; the source of the fact is the presence of
previousCloseOutcome in the event payload, see T003);
recipient — the recipient's relation to the issue at the moment of the event; digestRecipient — the relation
of the digest: a digest is addressed to a person, not to an issue, so 'is this their digest'
is derived from no relation to a single issue;
expect    — the expectation: outcome (reason|audit_only|no_reason_for_recipient|unmapped),
reason (only with outcome=reason) and whether the recipient falls into the AUDIENCE of each
channel. feed/push here is the registry audience, not a user setting:
materialisation of a row is decided by the composition 'channel enabled AND recipient in the
audience', and the second half of that composition is checked here.

cases.note: pair table: issue created already with an assignee | new assignee | Issue assignment
pair table: issue created already with an assignee | issue and project subscribers | New issue
assignee who is also subscribed: one reason per pair, the more specific one wins
pair table: issue created without an assignee | subscribers | New issue
a stranger recipient of a create event: no reason, and that is not a failure
pair table: edit that changed the assignee | new assignee | Issue assignment
pair table: edit that changed the assignee | subscribers | Issue assignment
pair table: edit changed assignee and priority | new assignee | Issue assignment
pair table: subscribers receive Issue assignment — the reason's priority outranks «other edits»
pair table: edit changed only priority | subscribers | Other issue edits
pair table: assignee cleared | subscribers | Issue assignment, feed channel; no push — the addressee does not exist
edits of other fields produce no delivery: the event lives in the journal, and that is not a failure
the feed of «Delegated issue status» is ANY status change on a watched issue
push — to the creator and only when the issue is really delegated
the creator themselves changed the status: there is no delegation, the push audience does not include them
creator and assignee are the same person: the issue is delegated to nobody
sk-489, R-7: the repeated close changed the outcome — the author is addressed with the outcome_changed reason, so they do not get the status row (otherwise two notifications about one action)

sk-489, R-7, the distinguishing case: the author is SUBSCRIBED to their own issue. The branch reads 'subscriber OR author', so an implementation that checked only 'not the author' would return the status row to them as a subscriber — IsCreator must win over IsSubscriber
sk-489: a subscriber who is not the author gets the status row as usual — for them an outcome change is not a reason but a detail of the close
sk-489 / US-3: the outcome of a closed issue changed — the reason is addressed to the requester, both channels are their audience

sk-489: the author CHANGED THE OUTCOME THEMSELVES. The registry answers with the same reason and the same audience — the silence for them comes not from here but from the recipient SELECTION (the own-action exclusion, selectFanOutCandidateSQL), and is checked through the real writer by case (c) of matrix row 43. The case is written exactly so, to make visible which layer owns the rule
sk-489: a subscriber who is not the author gets no separate row about an outcome change — there is no reason on any channel
sk-489, edge: the assignee of a closed issue is not an addressee. The outcome is edited FOR them, not by them, and the requester must learn about it
acceptance with the explicit tool | creator | Issue accepted by assignee
the same acceptance goes to a subscriber in the feed
pair table: acceptance stamped automatically (claim, self-assign, creating an issue on yourself) | anyone | no reason
claiming an issue gets no reason of its own — it arrives as a delegated-issue status change
closing also arrives as a status change; it has no reason of its own
archival is excluded from the registry as a matter of fact: there is no delivery for it on any path
creating a dependency is excluded from the registry — a journal event
deleting a dependency — same
a manual unclaim carries the sibling issue.status_changed; there must not be a second notification for one action (INV-6)
lock release by the stale-lock reaper — reason «Automatic unclaim», off by default, the reason has no push
creating a comment | to subscribers | Comment (off by default)
an attachment is projected onto the issue and belongs to the Attachment reason (INV-13)
parent change | to subscribers | Moved in the tree
a mention in a comment is addressed and arrives on both channels
a mention in the issue text — the same reason
a subscriber who was not mentioned does not get the mention reason: mention delivery is produced by addressing, not by subscription (INV-8)
a reminder rang | to the owner | Reminder; the feed channel is inapplicable (SC-022)
someone else's reminder is not addressed to a subscriber
setting a reminder is a journal event; it has no delivery
editing a comment produces no delivery
removing an attachment deliberately does not notify
labels — journal
project administration is not a reason
US-4: unaccepted digest, addressee — reason «Unaccepted issue — reminder», push only
a digest is addressed — an issue subscriber does not receive it, and that is not a failure
US-5: unreviewed digest, addressee — reason «Awaiting review — reminder», push only
addressing of the second category is checked separately from the first — categories are not merged (R-4)
edge: the digest addressee is also the creator of issues in it — still exactly one reason, the digest one
INV-2: a review mark is a journal record, there is no reason even for the author
INV-2: the assignee does not learn about the mark on any channel — journal silence, not unmapped
INV-2: flipping the review-required flag produces no delivery
INV-2: an issue subscriber does not learn about the flag change either
edge: an event with a delivery path the registry cannot name — observable unmapped, not a silent loss
